tools.description: Analyze whether a candidate firewall rule overlaps with an existing ruleset. Detects exact duplicates, shadowed rules, action conflicts, and partial overlaps. Two input modes: (1) vendor-native configs via vendor + ruleset_payload + candidate_rule_payload, or (2) pre-normalized JSON via existing_rules + candidate_rule. Use parse_policy first to inspect parser output before analysis.

candidate_position.description: Optional 1-based intended insertion position of the candidate rule.

candidate_rule.description: Single normalized rule object (same schema as existing_rules elements). Example: {"id": "candidate", "position": 1, "action": "permit", "source_addresses": ["10.20.35.76/32"], "destination_addresses": ["172.16.20.0/24"], "services": [{"protocol": "tcp", "ports": "6379"}]}. Required for Mode 2.

candidate_rule_payload.description: Single candidate rule in vendor-native text format (e.g. one ACL line for IOS). Required for Mode 1.

context_objects.description: Optional JSON string with supplemental object definitions (address groups, service objects).

existing_rules.description: Array of normalized rule objects from parse_policy output. Each object: {"id": "rule_1", "position": 1, "action": "permit"|"deny", "source_addresses": ["10.0.0.0/8"], "destination_addresses": ["any"], "services": [{"protocol": "tcp", "ports": "443"}], "source_zones": ["any"], "destination_zones": ["any"], "applications": ["any"]}. Required for Mode 2.

os_version.description: Optional OS version string for parser selection.

ruleset_payload.description: Complete firewall config in vendor-native text format (e.g. full 'show access-lists' output for IOS). Required for Mode 1.

vendor.description: Vendor identifier. One of: "panos", "asa", "ftd", "ios", "iosxr", "checkpoint", "juniper", "junos", "sros", "fortios". Required for Mode 1 (vendor-native).

tools.name: analyze_firewall_rule_overlap
tools.title: Analyze Firewall Rule Overlap

tools.description: Analyze multiple candidate rules against the same existing ruleset in a single call. More efficient than calling analyze_firewall_rule_overlap multiple times — existing_rules is parsed once and reused for each candidate. Use parse_policy first to get normalized rules, then pass all candidates at once.

candidate_rules.description: Array of candidate rule objects to analyze. Each object: {"id": "candidate-1", "position": 1, "action": "permit"|"deny", "source_addresses": ["CIDR"], "destination_addresses": ["CIDR"], "services": [{"protocol": "tcp", "ports": "443"}], "source_zones": ["any"], "destination_zones": ["any"], "applications": ["any"]}.

existing_rules.description: Array of normalized rule objects from parse_policy output. Parsed once and reused for all candidates.

tools.description: Parse a vendor-native firewall config and return normalized JSON rules. Use this to inspect what the built-in parser extracts — verify rule counts, object resolution, and address expansion before running overlap analysis. The output uses the same normalized schema accepted by analyze_firewall_rule_overlap.

context_objects.description: Optional JSON string with supplemental object definitions (address groups, service objects).

os_version.description: Optional OS version string for parser variant selection.

ruleset_payload.description: Complete firewall config in vendor-native text format. For IOS: paste the full 'show access-lists <name>' output. For PAN-OS: paste the full XML config tree.
